items.title: Bobby Johnson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998
items.q: But then Charlie and I joined a band, we joined the band together out in Queens, a show band.

ctx.x: I understand you had some pretty famous neighbors across the way.

Oh yeah. You heard of my neighbors. Well the great Charlie Parker lived directly across the street from us in the Dewey Square Hotel. And every night he’d practice scales, and so once my mother said, “You know I’ll really be glad when that guy learns how to play that thing.” Talking about this, what’s his name, Dick Wilson, the whole Andy Kirk band lived in a hotel called the Dewey Square Hotel that was directly across at 117th Street. As a matter of fact I took some of the musicians from here, and we paused in…
You had to start work at six at Ryan’s?
